brief: RBC's sentiment and valuation indicators suggest US stocks could stabilize soon, even if Thursday's 5.9% drawdown from the all-time high is not the final low, because the work is not yet "washed out": AAII sentiment, the US/non-US developed-market relative P/E, and big-cap forward P/E's are all near prior stress lows, but the Russell 2000's forward P/E has not fallen as far as its April 2025 tariff lows, a less oversold signal. RBC classifies the pullback as tier 1 (5-10%) in its four-tier framework and expects it to stay there, with the S&P 500 unlikely below 7000, unless AI-regulation risk to 2027 earnings worsens; the moment of truth comes in early calendar 1Q when companies issue year-ahead outlooks. Earnings sentiment must stabilize for P/E's to stop falling. Small Caps have outperformed Large Cap since mid-October, led by Utilities, REITs, Consumer Discretionary and Financials, a trade RBC continues to prefer so long as high-yield spreads and the VIX stay contained. Midterm exit polls flag the economy, cost of living and AI/data-center backlash as risks to the view that a divided Congress changes little.
